title: Endocytosis and exocytosis
caption: Cargo too big for any channel or carrier crosses wrapped in membrane. A phagocyte engulfs a whole bacterium; receptors in clathrin-coated pits gather LDL particles; and secretory vesicles fuse with the membrane to release enzymes. All three use ATP.
alt: A phospholipid bilayer with a bacterium being engulfed by phagocytosis, an LDL particle taken in by receptor-mediated endocytosis, and digestive enzymes leaving the cell by exocytosis, each in a vesicle.
description: Phagocytosis: the membrane flows around a bacterium and encloses it in a vesicle, which then fuses with lysosomes.
Receptor-mediated endocytosis: LDL particles carrying cholesterol bind receptors in clathrin-coated pits, which pinch off as vesicles.
Exocytosis: a vesicle of digestive enzymes fuses with the plasma membrane and releases them outside, adding its membrane to the surface.
All three use ATP to move vesicles and reshape the cytoskeleton.
